name: X-linked intellectual disability, Fichera type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and genetic diagnostic criteria for XLID Fichera type

criteria.description: Presence of moderate to severe intellectual disability
Characteristic facial dysmorphic features including prominent forehead, broad nasal bridge, and large ears
X-linked inheritance pattern with affected males and carrier females
Identification of pathogenic variants in the ZNF41 gene
Presence of behavioral abnormalities such as hyperactivity or autistic features

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of intellectual disability, characteristic facial dysmorphism, X-linked inheritance pattern, and pathogenic variant in ZNF41 gene
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for confirmation; clinical features may overlap with other XLID syndromes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Characteristic facial dysmorphism (prominent forehead, broad nasal bridge, large ears)
searchTerms: wide nose bridge and unusual face shape

common.symptomName: Behavioral abnormalities including hyperactivity and autistic-like features
Speech delay or absence of speech

laboratory: Possible mild metabolic abnormalities secondary to feeding difficulties
imaging: Brain MRI may show nonspecific cerebral atrophy or delayed myelination
genetic: Pathogenic variants in the ZNF41 gene located on X chromosome
other: Family history consistent with X-linked inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: May lack characteristic dysmorphism of Fichera type
Presence of CGG repeat expansion in FMR1 gene
Distinctive behavioral phenotype including hand flapping

redFlags: Severe intellectual disability with early developmental delay
Family history of affected males with carrier females
Characteristic facial dysmorphism suggestive of X-linked intellectual disability
references: Fichera M et al. X-linked intellectual disability: clinical and molecular characterization of the Fichera type. Am J Med Genet A. 2002.
Orphanet: X-linked intellectual disability, Fichera type. Orphanet Report Series. 2023.
